title: check: one file_history per path costs minutes at kernel scale
description:
git-vouch:1270-1275 (registry_history) calls file_history once per people/tiers/revocations file and .sig. Each call is 4 git processes (git-vouch:282 rev-parse --is-shallow-repository, the per-path git log at 285, cat-file --batch-check and --batch in read_blobs at 241/251), and each git log walks the whole history. At kernel scale (606 people, about 2,424 people+tiers files) that is about 9,700 git runs per check, O(paths x commits).

Measured on a synthetic repo (3,000 linear commits, 2,424 paths, git fast-import): 20 paths' worth of those 4 processes took 2.04 s, i.e. about 100 ms per path, or about 245 s per check projected. One combined 'git log --full-history -c --raw --no-renames --no-abbrev -z --format="%H %ct %P" -- people tiers revocations anchors.json' over the same repo took 0.53 s. The ponytail at git-vouch:1270 ('a registry of thousands of files takes seconds') understates the ceiling by about two orders of magnitude. check is the merge gate and runs on every sync/export/query, so this is the dominant cost.

What goes wrong if it stays: check takes minutes per run once the registry has years of history, and each new commit makes every later run slower.

Fix (cheapest): run one git log over the four sources and bucket the raw lines by path. With --full-history, -c's per-file combined diff gives each path the same lines its single-path log would. Then run one cat-file --batch-check and one --batch over all blobs, and the shallow check once. The parser at 300-315 only drops its 'path != rel' assertion in favour of a dict. The merge log at 1235-1262 already has this multi-path shape. Until then, correct the ponytail's stated ceiling.
